fatal_errors: The cited AlNbTiZr evidence concerns corrosion under simulated PWR operating conditions, not oxidation in 1000–1100 °C steam, so it does not support the central high-temperature accident-performance claim.
The proposed Nb2Zr6O17/ZrO2 mediator is transferred from a different coating system and exposure regime; the target protection instead depends on a continuous Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 layer in AlTiCrZrNbTa.
The experiment does not specify temperature, duration, steam flow, coating thickness, or matched composition controls, preventing a decisive test under the relevant conditions.
explanation: The hypothesis is directionally aligned with the problem: it proposes a sputtered, approximately 10 at.% Al multicomponent coating and predicts reduced mass gain and oxygen penetration relative to uncoated and non-optimal-Al controls. However, it reconstructs a different material system, deposition method, substrate, and oxide mechanism. Most importantly, E1 and E2 support AlNbTiZr behavior under normal PWR corrosion conditions rather than severe high-temperature steam oxidation, while E3 provides only broad contextual support. Thus the asserted accident-temperature protection is an unsupported extrapolation. The proposed experiment has useful comparative measurements and an explicit falsification rule, but its unspecified exposure parameters and reliance on unvalidated oxide phases substantially reduce discriminability.
